articles.title: Finding the right EastMallBuy QC photo before buying a spreadsheet find
articles.description: Trace a spreadsheet result to the live product page and check whether the available QC image actually shows your selected option.

sections.heading: Follow the listing through to the selectable option
paragraphs: Imagine finding a linen shirt in a spreadsheet. The thumbnail shows a white shirt, but the live page also sells ivory, cream and an unbleached version with contrasting buttons. Save the original seller link and the option text for the one you intend to order. When two versions share the same main photograph, a product title and a thumbnail alone cannot tell you which one the checkout will request.

sections.heading: Look for earlier orders in the product's QC section
paragraphs: EastMallBuy explains that its product pages can include QC images when another user has already bought that product. Open the gallery associated with the live offer and see whether the pictured label, construction or colour corresponds to the option you chose. If you cannot determine the variant, treat the photo as a view of the listing generally. Do not infer that your exact size was measured or that today's stock uses identical materials.

sections.heading: Read the picture for one practical question
paragraphs: If your concern is whether the buttons contrast, find a close view of the placket. If you need to know how long the shirt is, look for a tape and both endpoints. A distant image of a garment on a warehouse surface seldom settles measurement questions. Lighting can also make similar shades look different. EastMallBuy's inspection policy identifies colour differences and measurement errors among the limits of its standard inspection service.

sections.heading: Decide what you can leave until arrival
paragraphs: A missing pre-purchase gallery means you have less visual evidence. It does not establish that the listing has failed inspection. Decide whether the seller's specification is adequate, whether to ask a question, or whether to choose a better-documented item. If you proceed, keep the option you actually submitted. Once your own item is stored, compare its warehouse images with that recorded selection before releasing it for international shipment.

sections.heading: Identify what kind of photograph you have
paragraphs: EastMallBuy's product-page help explains where its earlier-buyer QC section comes from. On an independent finds page, however, a gallery can contain several kinds of images. There may be seller promotional shots, detail photos, option thumbnails and images associated with previous warehouse inspections. Before using a photograph as evidence, establish which set it belongs to and whether the page identifies the source listing. A studio image against a clean background could be useful for seeing the intended design while offering no evidence of how a previous unit actually arrived.

A practical test is to ask what the picture could prove even if the caption were missing. If it shows a shirt laid flat with the buttons visible, you can count the visible buttons on that sample. You cannot recover its size, order date or seller from the picture alone. Use labels and links supplied with the gallery to establish what can be matched. When the page omits an association, write “variant unconfirmed” rather than quietly filling in the missing link yourself.

sections.heading: Look for the characteristic that separates your options
paragraphs: Imagine a seller offering two travel pouches in the same colour. The small version has one zipper and an interior sleeve. The larger one has two zippers and an internal divider. If your main requirement is the divider, a picture of the green exterior settles very little. Find a view of the inside, compare it with the specific seller option and check that there is an actual second compartment. A view of a similar item in another size is still weak evidence for a feature that changes with size.

The useful question can be simpler for another product. If every variation of a notebook uses the same binding but buyers can choose a blue or black elastic closure, an exterior image with the closure visible may answer your question immediately. Concentrating on the distinguishing feature makes a five-image gallery more useful than scrolling through dozens of unrelated photographs. It also makes a later request for additional evidence much more precise.

sections.heading: Account for the camera and the measuring method
paragraphs: With clothing, apparent differences may come from camera angle, folds and lighting. A sleeve stretched diagonally across an image can look longer than one resting beside a body panel. For an actual length comparison, identify the start point, end point and tape units. If the seller's size guide measures shoulder seam to cuff but the previous buyer measured from the neckline, both results could be correct while describing different dimensions.

Colour deserves similar care. A cream fabric photographed under cool lighting can appear whiter than it would next to a white garment outdoors. Look for a known reference in the frame, but do not assume that a warehouse surface or label paper provides calibrated colour. If an exact dye match is essential for a coordinated outfit, an earlier buyer's image might reduce uncertainty without eliminating it. Decide whether that remaining uncertainty fits the purpose and price of your purchase.

sections.heading: Give a missing photograph the right amount of weight
paragraphs: A missing public QC image is more important when the unknown concerns a costly, hard-to-return or highly specific variation. For a common accessory with a clearly specified size and material, you may be willing to order using the seller description alone. For a gift whose presentation box has to fit a particular shelf, exterior box dimensions might be decisive. When the needed evidence is absent, ask whether the merchant can confirm that exact detail ahead of purchase.

Choose your next step according to how reversible it is. Saving an item for later costs little. Ordering an uncertain variant creates a purchase and may create domestic postage costs even if a seller later accepts a return. Submitting an unresolved item for international shipment introduces another stage. By deciding which point is your deadline for an acceptable answer, you can use both pre-purchase and warehouse images without treating them as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Build a comparison that stays useful after the listing changes
paragraphs: For each shortlisted item, keep the source URL, chosen option, unit price at the time you checked, the feature you verified and any open question. Describe the observation in your own words. For example, “Earlier photo shows two exterior zip pulls; interior divider not visible” is a better note than “QC looks good.” The first statement tells you what to inspect when your item reaches the warehouse. The second asks you to remember your own unstated criteria.

If you are comparing several similar sellers, keep their photos with the appropriate seller references. A photo linked to seller A cannot establish how seller B packs a parcel, even if their main pictures appear identical. Avoid putting an earlier buyer's image beside a different seller's row without a visible explanation in your own notes. When the source is unclear, retain it as a visual reference only.

sections.heading: Compare your own order at arrival
paragraphs: After purchase, switch from the public listing to the order associated with your account. Check whether the current image set belongs to your order and whether the number of pieces shown corresponds to the option you selected. If the item has only just been stored and photos are missing, EastMallBuy's warehouse photography help explains that uploads can lag storage. If a time-sensitive issue remains, contact support with the order number and receipt date.

Suppose the earlier gallery showed both zippers on a large pouch, but your own photo shows a single zipper. Start by verifying the size written in the order. Then ask for the visible label or another angle if needed. Give support the specific discrepancy: the selected large version and the one visible zipper. This lets the warehouse distinguish a missing feature from an image that simply hides the second pull. Make the parcel decision after that practical question has an answer.

articles.title: Why an EastMallBuy order can show Stored before its photos appear
articles.description: Distinguish an empty pre-order gallery from a missing image set on your own warehouse order.

sections.heading: Identify which gallery you are looking at
paragraphs: An EastMallBuy product page may contain images from earlier buyers. Your own order has a different purpose. It records the item that the warehouse has received for you. You might therefore see product-page photos before you purchase and still have no personal order photos immediately after storage. Conversely, an empty public gallery does not tell you whether the warehouse has photographed your particular item.

sections.heading: Read the item status first
paragraphs: The official status guide places Seller sent on the domestic journey from the seller to the warehouse. At that point, the warehouse cannot photograph a parcel it has yet to receive. Stored means the item is at the warehouse and can be submitted. EastMallBuy's missing-QC article specifically explains that photos are uploaded in sequence and may take a few hours to appear after storage. That advice addresses newly stored items, rather than a promise of a fixed upload time.

sections.heading: Use a short wait to prepare a focused check
paragraphs: Before refreshing the gallery, note the expected colour, size, quantity and any separately ordered part. If the order is for a set, verify how many pieces the chosen option includes. If several boxes share one seller reference, check whether each has its own receiving record. This makes it easier to identify a genuine missing photograph when the images appear.

sections.heading: Decide when to contact support
paragraphs: If the item has been stored for some time and images are still absent, give support the item order number, storage time and the exact gallery that remains empty. Ask whether photography is pending or the photos are attached to another item record. If the seller's return period is approaching, explain the deadline and keep the item out of the international parcel until the outstanding concern is resolved.

sections.heading: Follow the order through three different views
paragraphs: Take a buyer who saves a product today, orders it tomorrow and sees it warehoused several days later. The public product page, the buying order and the final parcel each have a different purpose. A public QC gallery can show another buyer's earlier unit. The purchase record belongs to the item ordered for this customer. A parcel record describes one or more warehouse items grouped for overseas delivery. Looking at the wrong one can make perfectly normal progress resemble missing photography.

Start on the purchasing order and check the item reference, selected variation and most recent status. If two orders use the same product link, compare their individual references instead of expecting one gallery to identify both. A screenshot of the public page showing no earlier QC may explain why you lacked evidence at purchase. It is not proof that the warehouse failed to produce the pictures for the later private order.

sections.heading: Distinguish receiving from a completed photo review
paragraphs: EastMallBuy's status guide places Stored after domestic seller shipment. Its separate note about missing images explains that individual gallery updates can follow storage. These pages answer different questions. One tells you where the goods are in the workflow and another tells you why the newly stored record can look incomplete. Neither gives reason to assume that the buyer has already reviewed the unit or approved it for overseas dispatch.

This matters for buyers building a parcel quickly. Suppose a shirt arrives on the same morning you intend to submit three older items. You might be able to select it without yet having the visual evidence you want. Ask whether it is more sensible to hold the new item briefly, submit only the accepted items, or wait on the combined parcel. Use the shipping and storage implications of those actual choices. A selectable checkbox alone is weak evidence that the product matches your specification.

sections.heading: Rule out an order-reference mix-up
paragraphs: Two almost identical orders may have different timestamps, colours or quantities. If a black sleeve and a navy sleeve share the same main thumbnail, the public name shown on both rows might be identical. Open the stored row directly and compare the selected option and receipt date with your order confirmation. When you see photos on one and none on the other, establishing which entry is actually in the warehouse can resolve the issue before support is involved.

Split deliveries create a related problem. A merchant selling a set might dispatch one part separately, or several orders might reach the warehouse in one domestic package. Compare the quantities shown as received for the relevant item. If you are unsure whether another carton is outstanding, ask about it explicitly. A request for “the missing photo” is difficult to resolve when the physical item expected in that photo may still be in domestic transit.

sections.heading: Prepare a review that the available photos can answer
paragraphs: Make a short list of requirements visible without professional testing. For a set of organizers, that may be the number of trays, the colour option and whether the largest tray has a lid. Confirm which of these the seller offered. When the photos appear, compare the observed feature with the selected variation. If an overhead photo hides a lid underneath the tray, record the ambiguity instead of treating it as an established omission.

For electrical equipment, sealed models and products where performance matters, EastMallBuy's inspection policy limits the scope of ordinary inspection. A new photo may clarify a printed model number or external damage while leaving operation untested. Ask about the specific question and feasible checks. Repeatedly waiting for more standard photos is unlikely to produce a functional diagnosis that the service never undertook to perform.

sections.heading: Escalate with a timeline and a precise question
paragraphs: A support message can read, “Order [reference], option [seller text], changed to Stored at [time and date]. The item record still shows no warehouse images. Can you check whether photography is pending or whether its images were posted under a different reference?” This wording distinguishes a delay from an order mismatch and gives the team a searchable record. If you have already checked an app and the website, mention that fact and the account entry used.

If a seller's return period may end soon, include the warehouse arrival time and the outstanding issue without pre-judging it. For example, explain that you need to confirm whether the two-piece version was received. Ask what action will preserve your options while checks are pending. Keep the order private and share evidence only through the platform's own channels. Seller receipts and shipping labels can contain address and account details irrelevant to a public discussion.

sections.heading: Act on what the images eventually show
paragraphs: A useful image review ends with a decision rather than a collection of pictures. If the received option, count and condition fit the order and all essential questions are answered, the item may be ready to join the rest of your parcel. If an important feature is hidden, request the smallest additional check that would settle it. If a visible label conflicts with your order confirmation, save the relevant images and raise that discrepancy on the purchase record promptly.

Keep your notes specific to the evidence. “Three trays visible; lid underneath cannot be seen” is easier to follow up than “QC incomplete.” If support confirms the lid with a targeted view, you can close that question without rechecking every unrelated feature. This approach also makes past orders easier to understand months later: a stored date shows when the item arrived, a gallery records what the camera captured and your own review records why you chose to ship it.

If two items ultimately share a parcel, retain both individual order references in the parcel notes. That small detail lets you trace a confirmed warehouse finding to the correct purchase even when the later shipment contains several nearly identical variants.

articles.title: Reading EastMallBuy order statuses from purchase request to storage
articles.description: Use the item's status to work out whether the next update belongs to the agent, the merchant or the warehouse.

sections.heading: Under process and Purchased answer different questions
paragraphs: When you pay for a purchase request, the seller may not yet have received the order. EastMallBuy uses Under process for a request waiting for the purchasing step. Purchased means the purchase has been placed and seller dispatch is still pending. If you accidentally selected the wrong option, contact the agent immediately with the precise correction. Waiting for Seller sent adds a domestic shipment to a problem that may once have been simpler to resolve.

sections.heading: Seller sent refers to the first delivery
paragraphs: This status describes goods leaving the merchant for EastMallBuy's warehouse. A merchant's domestic tracking number belongs to this part of the journey. A domestic carrier may show delivered before the warehouse has finished identifying, inspecting and recording each item. If the carrier record and account status remain out of step, present the order number and domestic tracking details together so the receiving team can match them.

sections.heading: Stored opens a new decision
paragraphs: At storage, review the goods that arrived and their available photos. An item being ready for parcel submission does not automatically mean the warehouse has sent it abroad. Consider whether the order is complete, its return conditions and any other items you intend to consolidate. With several purchases in one account, make the decision item by item. One slow seller does not reset an earlier item's storage date.

sections.heading: Switch to the parcel record after submission
paragraphs: EastMallBuy also uses parcel and transfer statuses. Its help entry for Not reviewed describes warehouse review and packing after parcel submission. The transfer glossary uses Processing for handling and Mailed for international transport. Before asking why an order is stuck, identify whether the label is on an item or on a parcel. Quote the label, reference number and time it last changed so support can identify the correct stage.

sections.heading: Trace a shopping basket with items from several merchants
paragraphs: Imagine buying a notebook, a case and a desk mat. Your account might show Purchased for the notebook, Seller sent for the case and Stored for the mat on the same morning. Each line describes a separate purchase from a merchant. The basket is not moving as one physical parcel. Open the item that concerns you and read its own purchase reference and last update. A screenshot of the whole basket can hide which seller still needs to act.

Decide the action for each row. A purchase that needs a variant correction belongs with the agent handling its merchant order. A domestic package already sent may require a carrier trace before the warehouse can identify it. A stored item can be reviewed for contents and condition while the other two are moving. If you intend to consolidate the three, keep a separate parcel-planning note. That plan does not change their individual statuses or their separate storage dates.

sections.heading: Read a time estimate as an estimate for one leg
paragraphs: EastMallBuy's glossary gives typical timings for purchasing and for domestic seller dispatch to reach the warehouse. These are descriptions of stages, not a guaranteed total from clicking pay to delivery abroad. An item can be ready for purchase while the merchant still has to confirm an option or release stock. Domestic transit may end with a signature before warehouse registration is complete. Packing and international transport come afterwards and have their own records.

For a useful enquiry, state when the particular status started and what evidence you already have. “Purchased three days ago; can the merchant confirm dispatch for the blue option?” asks an answerable question. “Where is my international parcel?” is premature if the goods are still on the merchant's premises. When comparing two orders, compare the same stage and allow for different merchants or order conditions. Matching payment dates do not guarantee matching dispatch dates.

sections.heading: Investigate an apparent mismatch between two screens
paragraphs: The domestic carrier might say a box has been delivered while the EastMallBuy order still says Seller sent. First confirm that you are viewing the carrier number belonging to this item, not a different order from the same seller. Check whether the seller split the order into several boxes. Look for a receiving timestamp and review any account messages about identification or inspection. A physical handoff and an inventory update can be separate events.

If the mismatch persists, provide the merchant order number, item reference, carrier name, domestic tracking number, delivery time and a concise description of the expected contents. If there are multiple cartons, identify the one you want investigated. For forwarding orders, include the forwarding reference. Those details allow the receiving team to trace a box. A public tracking screenshot without an order reference may leave them unable to identify which account inventory should contain it.

sections.heading: Interpret Submitted alongside the actual parcel details
paragraphs: A stored item may be selected for an international parcel. Once submitted, follow the parcel's own review, payment and dispatch information rather than repeatedly checking its former seller shipping line. EastMallBuy describes Not reviewed as a post-submission warehouse step before final freight. An item being marked Submitted therefore does not by itself certify that the overseas carrier has accepted the complete parcel.

Record which item references you included at submission. If the case stores late, it might never have been selected for the parcel containing the mat. When the international parcel appears, compare its listed contents against your intended selection. This simple reconciliation is especially useful when the account contains two versions of the same product. One item remaining in storage could be an intentional hold or an omission you can still raise before dispatch.

sections.heading: Distinguish a seller change from a shipment change
paragraphs: Suppose you notice that the paid purchase shows the wrong size. Under process suggests that support may still be able to change the purchasing instruction, but you need confirmation before assuming the request was caught in time. Purchased indicates that communication with the merchant may already be required. Stored means the specific unit has arrived and the issue may need the warehouse return or exchange process. If the unit has entered a parcel, the parcel status matters as well.

Make one request that identifies both the mistake and the desired outcome. “Order A shows small; I intended medium. Please tell me whether the merchant can amend the purchase before dispatch” is more useful than a vague cancellation instruction covering the whole basket. If the correction is time-sensitive, keep the reply and check the actual selected specification. A support acknowledgement is not yet confirmation that the seller changed the item.

sections.heading: Turn an update into a next decision
paragraphs: Once an item is stored, check the available image set and seller specification, then decide whether it is accepted, needs more evidence or should be raised with the merchant. Once a combined parcel is ready, check its destination, route, selected items and packing. After the international handoff, switch to the carrier reference linked to that parcel. This keeps you from asking a warehouse photographer to trace a carrier or asking a merchant why a consolidated parcel has no overseas scan.

If an issue remains unresolved, maintain a small timeline with four columns in your own notes: date, exact status text, reference number and who can act next. Populate it with observed events instead of guesses about what probably happened. When a support response arrives, add the confirmed event and the next promised action separately. You will then have enough information to follow up at the right stage without re-explaining the entire purchase or mistaking the progress of another item for your own.

sections.heading: Record the next action, not just the next date
paragraphs: If the seller promises to dispatch later, record the date you will check for the domestic tracking number. If the parcel is waiting for warehouse review, look for a freight or packing update instead. Choosing the observable event in advance makes a missed update easier to investigate and keeps the item purchase and international shipping stages separate.

articles.title: Calculating EastMallBuy volumetric weight using its ETL example
articles.description: Work through the official example divisor and see which measurements actually change a parcel's weight comparison.

sections.heading: Measure a packed rectangular box
paragraphs: Use the outer length, width and height of the complete packing, in the unit the shipping line specifies. A seller's shoe size, a folded garment's dimensions and the unboxed product length are poor substitutes. EastMallBuy's help page gives an ETL example using centimetres and dividing cubic centimetres by 8,000 to obtain kilograms. That divisor belongs to the example. Read the current details for the route you select.

sections.heading: Work through a hollow parcel
paragraphs: Suppose a packed carton measures 50 by 40 by 30 centimetres and weighs 4 kilograms on the scale. Its volume is 60,000 cubic centimetres. Dividing by 8,000 gives 7.5 kilograms. In the official example's comparison, the volumetric figure is higher. A calculator filled with only the 4-kilogram reading would miss the impact of those dimensions. This calculation illustrates weight treatment, not a quoted price or guaranteed acceptance.

sections.heading: Test the dimension you can realistically change
paragraphs: If the same hypothetical box can be repacked to 50 by 40 by 20 centimetres, the result is 5 kilograms by volume. That would still exceed a 4-kilogram scale reading. If a second box of the original size weighs 9 kilograms instead, its scale reading is already higher than 7.5. Reducing its dimensions alone may leave its weight basis unchanged. Check any route rounding, minimum charge or packaging service cost in the actual quote.

sections.heading: Decide which packaging has a purpose
paragraphs: EastMallBuy suggests considering vacuum packing for down clothing or removing or folding boxes where appropriate. A compressible jacket and a rigid collector's box deserve different instructions. Identify whether the retail box is needed and whether a protective insert can safely be removed. After consolidation the platform's terms say measurements can change. Use the warehouse's packed result for the final comparison.

sections.heading: Find the break-even box height
paragraphs: You can turn the ETL example around to answer a more practical packing question. Imagine the scale reads 6 kilograms and a rigid base fixes two outer dimensions at 50 and 40 centimetres. What height would bring the calculated volume weight down to the scale weight? Multiply 6 by 8,000 and divide the result by 50 times 40. The result is 24 centimetres. Above that height, the volume figure is greater than 6 kilograms. At that height, the two figures meet. Below it, the scale reading is already the larger number under this comparison.

This gives the warehouse a meaningful question. If the goods fit safely in a 24-centimetre-high box, reducing a 30-centimetre carton might matter. If the carton can only be reduced from 25 to 24.5 centimetres, the theoretical change is small. Whether it changes the price depends on the tariff and billing increment offered for the route. There is little value in asking for an arbitrary “smaller box” until you know which dimension controls the outcome.

sections.heading: Compare a combined parcel with two separate cartons
paragraphs: Consider two illustrative parcels. A carton of soft clothing measures 40 by 30 by 24 centimetres and weighs 2.8 kilograms. Its ETL-example volume weight is 3.6 kilograms. A small parcel of books measures 25 by 20 by 16 centimetres and weighs 2.2 kilograms. Its volume weight is 1 kilogram. Taken separately, the larger weight figure for each is 3.6 and 2.2 kilograms respectively. Their sum is 5.8 kilograms before any route-specific rounding.

Now suppose the warehouse can put both groups into one carton measuring 40 by 32 by 28 centimetres, with a final scale reading of 5.3 kilograms including the new box. Its volume weight is 4.48 kilograms, so the scale figure is larger. That looks promising, but the calculation alone does not show the money saved. Ask the calculator for the eligible routes and both actual price configurations. Two parcels might pay two opening charges, one combined parcel might exceed a limit, or protective services might add a fee. Use those outputs when deciding whether to consolidate.

There is a second practical question in this example. Could dense books damage delicate clothing or crush a fitted accessory? Give the packer a description of the contents. If dividers or another carton are necessary, the original dimensions no longer apply. Rerun the calculation with the packing you would genuinely accept.

sections.heading: Spot unit mistakes before comparing amounts
paragraphs: An outer height of 240 millimetres must be entered as 24 centimetres in the official example. Entering 240 with the other two dimensions in centimetres makes the result ten times too large. A similar error arises when a scale displays grams while the quote expects kilograms. Record both the number and the unit rather than relying on memory as you move between a seller page, warehouse record and freight calculator.

As a quick check, compare the size to a familiar box and look at the order of magnitude. A 40-by-30-by-20-centimetre carton has a volume of 24,000 cubic centimetres. Under the illustrative divisor it gives 3 kilograms. If your worksheet reports 3,000 kilograms for that parcel, check the scale conversion and the units applied to each dimension before disputing the carrier result. If only one quote differs, inspect its route rules as well.

sections.heading: Put the estimate next to the packed record
paragraphs: In a simple worksheet, give one row to each packing option. Record the route, destination, item's packing requirements, outer dimensions, real weight, divisor used, computed volume weight and the quoted total. Include the time you checked and whether the measurements were estimated or supplied by the warehouse. When a box is repacked, keep the old row. Replacing the figures makes it difficult to explain which change produced a lower or higher quote.

Give the difference the correct unit. Going from 7.5 kilograms to 5 kilograms in the example removes 2.5 kilograms of calculated volume weight. It does not save 2.5 kilograms of physical goods, and it does not establish a particular price reduction. If a charge seems unchanged, ask which weight and tariff bracket the live quote uses. A clear screen capture of the route and box inputs is more helpful than a photo of the unpacked merchandise.

sections.heading: Decide what evidence would change your choice
paragraphs: For a plain jacket that already folds flat, you may be comfortable authorizing compression if the warehouse expects a meaningful reduction in height. For a gift set in a presentation box, a visible dent might defeat the purpose of the purchase. State whether the packaging may be discarded, folded, compressed or must be protected. Ask about the protective outer size if you need the retail box intact. A cheaper quote for a configuration you would reject is irrelevant to the choice.

If two packing methods remain plausible, compare the higher of the two weight figures for each, then the actual quoted fees and terms. Prefer the arrangement that preserves the item and meets your budget. Keep the accepted option with the parcel reference, especially if you intend to compare it with a later warehouse measurement. This is how an initially rough weight estimate becomes an auditable shipping decision.

When recording an estimated box shape, distinguish a genuine outer measurement from a sum of catalogue sizes. For example, stacking two shoe boxes adds their heights only when they are placed flat on top of one another. Putting them side by side may increase the width and leave the height nearly unchanged. There will also be clearance for padding. If the warehouse has not yet packed the items, test both plausible arrangements and label the results as estimates. A range makes it easier to judge whether the available budget is robust to a small change in carton size. Once you have the measured box, replace the range in your final comparison with the figure the platform actually uses and keep the earlier estimates for reference.

articles.title: EastMallBuy storage deadlines for normal and unmatched parcels
articles.description: Identify which clock applies when an ordinary purchase is stored or an incoming forwarding parcel has not been matched.

sections.heading: Start with the event that starts the clock
paragraphs: EastMallBuy's storage article describes a normal period of 90 days from warehouse status. The same article describes a 60-day period for abnormal incoming packages, such as a signed-for delivery without a submitted order or sufficient logistics information. The start event for that second case is signature. A parcel can therefore have a deadline even when nothing obvious appears in the account's normal inventory list.

sections.heading: Build a short receiving record for each delivery
paragraphs: For a regular purchase, keep the order number and warehouse-entry date alongside the item. For a forwarding delivery, also retain the original merchant receipt, domestic carrier and tracking number. Suppose a seller sends three items in two cartons. Record two tracking references and the contents of each. If one never appears in storage, support can investigate that one carton without confusing it with the delivery already identified.

sections.heading: Prioritize the oldest item before consolidating
paragraphs: Lay out the dates for the items you are waiting to combine. A newly stored accessory does not restart an older coat's storage period. Compare a partial shipment with waiting for the delayed merchant, taking account of whether the new item has actually shipped. If your account displays a different deadline or customer service gives an order-specific instruction, confirm the applicable date directly. The platform's terms refer customers to the page description or service notice.

sections.heading: Resolve unidentified packages early
paragraphs: EastMallBuy warns that unmatched parcels may be impossible to associate with a customer for reminders and that expired goods can be disposed of. If a domestic carrier confirms delivery but the item cannot be linked to your account, supply the tracking number, recipient details from the order and signature time through the private support channel. Ask for confirmation that the package is matched to your order and check the resulting account entry.

sections.heading: Build a calendar that starts on the right date
paragraphs: Imagine paying for a sweater on the first of a month, seeing the seller send it on the fourth and finding it marked in the warehouse on the seventh. For ordinary storage, EastMallBuy's guidance points to that last stage. If you enter the payment date in a column labelled warehouse arrival, your reminder will be inaccurate even if it happens to be early. For a separately purchased item that was signed for but cannot be matched to a forwarding record, the signature is the important event in the platform's abnormal-package guidance. Record the event's name along with its date.

Consider keeping three different fields: what the carrier last reported, what the EastMallBuy account shows, and the deadline confirmed for this order. If the last field is unknown, mark it as unknown and ask about it. A date calculated from a generic policy is useful for setting a reminder. An account-specific deadline can reflect information your calculation did not include. If the two disagree, seek confirmation before making travel plans or paying to hold other goods.

sections.heading: Work backwards from the oldest item
paragraphs: Assume a coat, two books and a small accessory are intended for one shipment. The coat is approaching its displayed deadline, both books are already stored, and the accessory is still waiting for its seller to dispatch. Ask what the combined parcel achieves. Perhaps the books need stronger protection than the coat, or the accessory is so small that shipping it later alone would be expensive. Price the actual alternatives, with the correct destination and eligible routes, before deciding to wait.

Now consider the evidence behind the accessory's timeline. A merchant estimate, a domestic tracking number with no movement and a confirmed warehouse scan each support a different degree of confidence. They should not all lead you to spend the same number of remaining days. Set yourself a decision date ahead of the storage limit. On that day, review whether the new item has actually advanced. A small potential freight saving rarely justifies allowing a valuable item to expire by accident.

sections.heading: Know what a delivery signature does and does not identify
paragraphs: A receiving signature ties a tracking number to a carrier event. It does not necessarily tell the warehouse which customer ordered the goods, which order should receive them or whether a merchant divided one purchase into multiple packages. This distinction matters most when you bought the item yourself. If you submit a forwarding reference with the wrong tracking number, the delivery may be physically present while the account record still has nothing to show.

To investigate, ask the merchant for the carrier and complete number for each shipment. Check for two similar numbers, a tracking number replaced after a label was cancelled or a dispatch assigned to a different carrier. Compare the exact address and reference used for shipping with those supplied in your account. Do not publicly post the warehouse label or personal contact details. Send the required information directly to the platform through its own support channel.

sections.heading: Prepare an evidence packet for an unmatched delivery
paragraphs: Start with the smallest set of details that uniquely identifies the package: your account's forwarding or order reference, the seller's order reference, the carrier and tracking number, delivery time and a concise item description. If available, add the merchant's packing details or an image of the actual shipping label with irrelevant personal information concealed. A product promotional image may identify the type of object but usually says little about the outer shipping carton the receiving team needs to locate.

Write the request as a matching problem: “The carrier shows one carton delivered on this date under this number. My forwarding entry shows no received package. Can you confirm whether the warehouse can match that carton to this entry?” If the order came in two boxes, state which is missing and which has already appeared. This prevents a reply confirming the first box from being mistaken for resolution of the second.

sections.heading: Avoid mixing the storage and return clocks
paragraphs: A stored item might still have weeks of warehouse time but very little time left to ask its merchant about an exchange. Conversely, a matched parcel could require attention before you have enough evidence to decide on an international line. Give these decisions separate rows or calendar reminders. In particular, review inspection photos promptly instead of interpreting the storage period as permission to postpone every other question about the purchase.

If you notice a wrong size or missing component, contact the order support channel with its specification, photo and warehouse receipt date. Ask for the merchant's applicable response period and any cost of sending the item back. That enquiry concerns the seller transaction. Choosing whether to consolidate your other accepted items concerns the parcel. Keeping the two threads separate avoids holding an entire shipment while the team is trying to resolve one small seller discrepancy.

sections.heading: Confirm the warehouse has acted
paragraphs: A support acknowledgement establishes that someone received your message. It does not on its own establish that a carton has been linked or that a storage deadline has changed. After receiving an update, reopen the inventory or forwarding record. Match the item, quantity and tracking reference. If the result is still ambiguous, request confirmation of the warehouse status and expiry date associated with the physical package.

When submitting goods for shipment, similarly save the waybill reference and look for any remaining payment or instructions the account requires. If your account shows an unsubmitted or unresolved parcel near its deadline, contact EastMallBuy promptly. In a group of staggered purchases, close the reminder for the item only after its own status changes. This preserves visibility of the remaining goods and keeps a single old, low-value order from being forgotten while attention moves to a newer purchase.

articles.title: Cancelling an EastMallBuy order after a waybill has been created
articles.description: Find the right reference and understand which part of a payment may still be reversible before international dispatch.

sections.heading: Identify the last completed operation
paragraphs: A buyer can pay a merchant, receive goods in the warehouse and submit a parcel on three different dates. These events matter because EastMallBuy's refund policy treats them as distinct stages. If a waybill already exists, find its number and current dispatch state immediately. A payment receipt alone cannot show whether the warehouse has already begun packing or handed the parcel to the carrier.

sections.heading: Contact the correct record without waiting for a scan
paragraphs: The published policy describes a pre-dispatch cancellation window normally within 24 hours after waybill submission, with cancellation potentially unavailable once packing or dispatch has begun. Treat this as a request that needs prompt confirmation. A tracking page without public updates does not prove the warehouse can still stop the parcel. Send the waybill number and specify whether the issue affects the complete shipment or one item inside it.

sections.heading: Separate freight reversal from the seller return
paragraphs: Stopping a parcel does not by itself return its goods to the merchant. The official policy distinguishes international freight on an undispatched parcel, services already performed and the merchant's rules for the goods. Ask which packing or consolidation fees have already been incurred. If the reason is an incorrect product, identify the item order, selected variant and relevant image and ask for the seller return or exchange steps after the parcel is stopped.

sections.heading: Check what actually happened
paragraphs: An acknowledgement of your message, a cancelled waybill and a successful refund are three separate events. Save the confirmation of each. Check where the item appears in warehouse inventory, whether the original waybill is inactive and where any refund is recorded. If dispatch has already taken place, consult the shipped-stage policy with the waybill and receipt to understand the remaining after-sales options.

sections.heading: Use the right reference for a change to a mixed parcel
paragraphs: Imagine a parcel containing five item orders, only one of which you want removed. The purchase number identifies that one item. The waybill identifies the parcel you are asking the warehouse to interrupt. Send both numbers and name the other items only as needed to make the requested action clear. If you actually want the other four shipped, say so, but ask whether the warehouse can change the item selection without cancelling and recreating the waybill. Do not assume the system supports an edit at the stage you reached.

A parcel-wide instruction can have bigger consequences than a seller return. “Cancel everything” might mean cancel five seller purchases, stop one international shipment, or reverse an available balance. A more precise request is “Please check whether waybill W can be stopped before dispatch because order A needs a return. I want to keep the other four goods.” This tells the team which physical action is urgent and which financial decisions can be reviewed after it has confirmed warehouse status.

sections.heading: Establish whether dispatch has actually happened
paragraphs: The refund policy distinguishes a waybill being created from the package being dispatched. A new tracking number does not settle the issue by itself. A warehouse may have generated a label while the goods remain on its premises, or a carrier may have collected the package without publishing its first visible scan. An account label such as Not reviewed is useful context, but support must confirm whether it can interrupt packing or dispatch in that particular case.

Write down the waybill submission time, the displayed status and when you filed the request. If support asks for an order number, identify whether they need the international waybill or the item purchase in question. Avoid creating a second waybill to correct the first without confirmation. Two active parcel records can make it harder to tell which set of packing and freight charges belongs to the goods.

sections.heading: Reconstruct the financial entries without double-counting
paragraphs: An international parcel may contain payments made at different stages. There is the merchandise amount paid for the items, domestic shipping to the warehouse, packing or other value-added work, and the international freight. In an undispatched cancellation, the policy addresses which shipping amounts may be refundable and which incurred services may remain. The seller's decision on the goods is a separate component. Ask for an itemized reply that names each affected charge rather than relying on one headline refund figure.

Use an invented example only to understand the arithmetic. Suppose the item cost 100 yuan, the international freight entry was 140 yuan and completed packing was listed separately at 12 yuan. If the parcel is stopped and the 140-yuan freight is reversed, that does not establish a 252-yuan refund. The packing service and the merchandise purchase still need their own resolution. If the 12 yuan was already included in another line, do not count it a second time. Reconcile against the actual account statement.

sections.heading: Compare the actions available before and after a stop
paragraphs: If the purpose is an address correction, ask support whether correction is possible on the existing record and confirm the exact final address privately. If a wrong item entered the parcel and you still want it, returning it to warehouse inventory may be enough. If the item is defective, attach purchase evidence and request the seller-stage remedy once it is accessible again. These are three different desired outcomes even though each begins with a request to stop dispatch.

Time spent establishing the reason should not delay the initial request when the warehouse window is short. Send a brief first message with the waybill, urgent issue and requested action. Follow up with any detailed proof once the warehouse acknowledges the enquiry. Keep the facts consistent across messages. If a second agent answers, the first reference and timestamps give them a clear record of what the team was originally asked to stop.

sections.heading: Recognize the limit after international dispatch
paragraphs: Once the parcel has been dispatched, EastMallBuy's policy generally does not allow ordinary cancellation. It describes separate after-sales routes for applicable warranty issues and damage or missing items at delivery. If support says the parcel has left, ask for the actual dispatch status and the available options that apply to the reason for your request. Expecting an undispatched-freight reversal after a confirmed handoff can send the enquiry down the wrong path.

If an item later arrives damaged, keep the outer packaging and evidence and consult the platform's applicable reporting times immediately. If the problem is simply that you changed your mind, do not report damage or loss that did not occur. The seller, carrier and platform handle different types of issues. Accurate information protects the credibility of a legitimate claim and helps avoid time spent collecting irrelevant evidence.

sections.heading: Confirm the final state of every affected item
paragraphs: After a successful intervention, check that the obsolete waybill is inactive, note any freight credit, and locate each retained item in the warehouse or its replacement parcel. For the item being returned, verify the seller's acceptance, requested domestic return cost and subsequent credit separately. If the remaining goods are to be shipped together, inspect the newly measured freight quote and verify that the removed item's reference is absent.

Make a final list of what still requires action. One parcel might be cancelled while the seller return is pending and four items remain stored with existing deadlines. Record those open tasks rather than closing the whole case when the first confirmation arrives. A well-documented cancellation finishes when you know where each item is, which charges were reversed, which work was already incurred and what must happen next to the goods you still want.

sections.heading: Check the new parcel against the original destination
paragraphs: When four retained goods are rebooked after removing a fifth, inspect the delivery address and option selection again. A new waybill can have its own service choices and quote. Keep both references with a note identifying which one is active so a later tracking enquiry does not accidentally refer to the cancelled shipment.

articles.title: Checking EastMallBuy insurance when a parcel contains forwarded goods
articles.description: Compare the origin of each item with the platform's insurance explanation before counting on compensation.

sections.heading: Start with who bought the goods
paragraphs: The buyer can use an agent to place a purchase or independently buy an item and send it to a forwarding warehouse. Two similar-looking products in one inventory screen may therefore have different histories. EastMallBuy publishes a specific notice excluding forwarding goods from its product-insurance compensation. Keep the original seller receipt and mark any independently purchased item as forwarded when reviewing coverage.

sections.heading: Read the named event as carefully as the benefit
paragraphs: EastMallBuy's insurance comparison discusses loss and customs seizure and distinguishes an item-value benefit from one that also includes freight. Read the terms offered with your actual parcel for eligibility, limits, exclusions and evidence. A description of loss compensation alone does not resolve a question about cosmetic damage, a seller supplying the wrong colour or a late arrival. Ask about the event you are actually concerned about.

sections.heading: Get a specific answer for a mixed parcel
paragraphs: Suppose the warehouse holds two agent purchases and one lamp you purchased yourself. Give support the three item references and identify the forwarded lamp. Ask which goods, if any, qualify under the applicable terms and how a claim for freight would be calculated if the package contains both types. Do this before authorizing shipment. A general answer about the existence of insurance leaves the important mixed-parcel question open.

sections.heading: Keep the evidence for the stage where a problem occurs
paragraphs: Hold onto purchase values, payment confirmations, packing lists and the accepted terms. For a delivery problem preserve the outside packaging, label and visible damage and consult the platform's deadlines promptly. The refund policy describes information required for damaged or missing arrivals, while the insurance terms define eligibility for covered events. A complete record helps the relevant party evaluate the case without promising any particular outcome.

sections.heading: Classify each line before buying a shipping add-on
paragraphs: Take an account containing a coat the agent bought from a Taobao merchant, a book bought through the same service and a desk stand you purchased independently and forwarded. All three could eventually occupy one outer box, yet the supporting purchase records differ. The platform's published exception for forwarded goods makes that distinction material. Make a list with the order reference, purchase channel, declared item value and actual receipt available for each. A picture of everything in the same warehouse does not establish identical eligibility.

If you are uncertain whether a particular order was an agent purchase or forwarding, check who paid the merchant and which workflow generated the warehouse entry. You may have funded the agent using your balance while the agent bought the goods on your behalf. That differs from paying the seller directly and entering a forwarding order only for transportation. Describe the facts to support rather than naming the service from memory.

sections.heading: Compare coverage for a defined loss
paragraphs: Start by writing down the event you want protection against. A complete package that never arrives, one missing component inside a delivered set, visible damage on arrival and a seller sending the wrong size are different events. EastMallBuy's comparison page specifically discusses loss and customs seizure. Its statement about those events cannot simply be carried over to breakage, delay or merchant mistakes. Consult the insurance terms associated with the available route and ask about any event important to your decision.

For example, the forwarding desk stand might have a finish that scratches easily. If your concern is surface damage, ask separately about protective packing and whether the event qualifies for any applicable compensation. Buying an add-on designed around another event may leave the real concern unresolved. Conversely, an eligible agent-purchased item in the same carton may have different terms. Keep each written answer with the item and the route referred to in the answer.

sections.heading: Understand the difference between a value and a reimbursement
paragraphs: Use purchase receipts to establish what was actually paid. A list price, a conversion shown on an independent spreadsheet, a seller's promotional figure and the amount you paid may differ. When comparing two benefits, check which amount the service recognizes and whether any limit, excluded charge or proof requirement applies. “Item value” is a category of cost; by itself it tells you little about how a particular claim would be assessed.

Consider an illustrative parcel with 250 yuan of agent-purchased goods, a separately forwarded item costing 80 yuan and freight of 110 yuan. Adding the three gives 440 yuan of personal expenditure. It does not establish a 440-yuan insured amount. Ask which portion of eligible merchandise is recognized, whether the forwarded item is excluded and under what condition freight could be considered. The example highlights the questions; only the applicable terms and evidence can determine the actual answer.

sections.heading: Ask about a mixed shipment in writing
paragraphs: A concise enquiry can say, “For planned parcel [reference], orders A and B were purchased through EastMallBuy and C was forwarded after I paid its merchant directly. Under this route and option, which goods qualify if the whole parcel is lost, and is international freight included?” If you are concerned about a different event, name it. Include the displayed product or route terms privately if the selected option is difficult to identify.

If the reply says simply “insurance available,” ask which part of your item list the answer covers. If the answer is that forwarded goods cannot be covered by the platform's product insurance, keep that fact visible in your budget. You might choose to send items separately for record-keeping, select stronger packing or accept a risk you understand. Separate packing does not transform an excluded purchase into an eligible one. Evaluate the real terms and cost for each alternative.

sections.heading: Preserve evidence during packing and delivery
paragraphs: Save the order confirmations, receipt amounts, parcel contents and the terms displayed when you chose the service. Record the shipping line and date. If the warehouse provides an image of packed goods, keep it with the waybill. That image can help establish what was prepared for shipment, but a photograph cannot by itself prove what happened during transport. For a missing item, compare the purchase and packing list with what you actually received.

At arrival, follow the platform's published instructions for inspection and reporting. Its refund policy has specific directions concerning outer packaging, evidence and time limits for missing or damaged goods. Keep the packaging and label while you document a genuine problem. Take wide views that identify the parcel and close views that show the issue, and provide them through private channels. If the parcel is delayed rather than declared lost, request a trace before assuming a loss benefit applies.

sections.heading: Route the request to the party that can investigate
paragraphs: If a seller sent the wrong variant and the warehouse evidence already showed it, the starting issue is with the merchant order. If a parcel has not had a public scan, the carrier and platform may need to trace a handoff. If EastMallBuy confirms an eligible event has occurred, ask for the applicable claim procedure, required documentation and deadline. These enquiries can run in sequence, but the first unanswered question should determine whom you contact.

Keep a final case record listing the event accepted, eligible items, recognized purchase amounts, freight treatment and eventual outcome. If liability or entitlement is disputed, retain the terms and case correspondence rather than relying on a marketing phrase detached from its route. This lets you compare future options using actual scope and evidence, instead of assuming that every product described as insurance offers the same protection to every item in a consolidated box.

sections.heading: Record the version of the terms you accepted
paragraphs: Save the date, route and exact coverage option shown when you submitted the shipment. If later help text is revised, the account record gives support a way to identify which offer was presented for your parcel. Keep sensitive order and payment details private while retaining enough information to distinguish that transaction from a later shipment on another line.
